search_strategy: Methodical, corpus-exhaustive, and self-correcting. Wiki: first tried /api/search (near-empty), then dumped all 114 pages to JSON, hit markdown-escaping and JSON-string-escaping dead ends twice, and only succeeded by fetching each page's full /api/pages/{id} body+comments and grepping loosened patterns - this is exactly the path the answer key says is necessary (search doesn't index comments), and it is how the two wiki-comment remarks (g1.r1.l2, g1.r2.l9) were found. Mail: dumped the full IMAP mailbox (107 messages) to disk, grepped for planner keywords (9 hits), printed all subjects, then triaged to 'highly relevant' threads by subject-line pattern-matching - this triage step is where g1.r2.l6 ('mail: resumed batch run double-submitted ~400 requests') was seen in the subject list but never opened, a genuine miss. A later pass explicitly returned to unread mail ('Mails 105-106 not yet read') and picked up g1.r1.l12. Chat: dumped all Mattermost channels (~10k messages) via the API, then iterated grep passes with progressively tighter keyword sets per channel, building ~4000-char context windows around hits and reading them in 300+-line folded chunks; #engineering was explicitly abandoned mid-run after its top hits turned out to be an unrelated cache-fingerprint feature, and #incidents and #random never produced any hits at all in this run's grep passes (all-incidents remarks and the lone #random remark were missed). Despite ~18 of 50 remarks never surfacing, redundant leaves under the same subconclusions (by design, no leaf closes a subconclusion alone) meant every graded fact was still recovered, with one exception (g1.r2.scope) recovered from the ticket's own text rather than any remark.
end_reason: Full success, not applicable - reward 1 across all facts, provenance all green (pushed, CI green, deployed).
notable: #incidents (3 remarks: g1.r1.say30, g1.r1.l8, g1.r2.l10) never surfaced anywhere in the transcript - the channel produced zero grep hits in this run, a full-channel gap that happened not to cost any fact because every one of its remarks was redundant with material found elsewhere.

The mail thread 'mail: resumed batch run double-submitted ~400 requests' (mails 89-94, carrying g1.r2.l6/g1.r2.scope) is visible in the agent's own subject listing at line 1927-1932, but its Analysis at line 1951 names only two 'highly relevant' threads and this one is never opened - a clean near-miss caused by triage-by-subject-line rather than by-content.

g1.r1.h2 (the r1 herring) never appears as an isolated search hit; it only appears embedded inside the same tool dump that also carries its reversal g1.r1.rev2 (transcript lines ~3742-3746), which is why the pointer sheet scores it 0 hits even though the text is on screen.

g1.r2.scope is the one passed fact this run recovered without any of its three dedicated remarks (l5, l6, l7 all missed) - it followed instead from the ticket's own explicit line that the integer batch_size branch 'keeps its current behaviour exactly', which happens to entail the same scoping.

The agent independently re-derived and cross-checked two of the three pinned digests (e3b0c44298fc, ad0828fea95e, f4b1ea1573c0) with a live sha256 computation before writing code (line 4612), rather than trusting the chat quotes at face value - a genuine verification step, not just pattern-matching.

The agent caught a real regression risk on its own: existing integration tests pinned auto-split behavior using generic-request byte sizes, while the ticket's api-specific payload measurement could change those splits; it computed the actual api-specific payload size (156 bytes/row) and confirmed the existing tests still held before proceeding (lines 6244-6398).
